page: Amazon Web Services m6g.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 32 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 model running at 2.5 GHz. The CPU configuration provides 32 vCPUs with a single thread per core, supported by 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the m6g.8xlarge in the average performance tier for most multi-core and database operations, though single-core execution shows some limitations. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 48,570.2 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,518.0, both falling within the average range. Redis SET operations reached 36.99 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput was measured at 32.53 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is weaker, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 950.0 and a Passmark memory score of 1,816.99, which are categorized in the bottom 25% of tested hardware.

The absence of local storage and dedicated GPU hardware limits this instance to workloads reliant on network-attached storage and CPU-only processing. While it demonstrates average capabilities in software compilation and multi-threaded decompression, its single-threaded compression and text processing performance are relatively weak. The hardware profile and resource density make it suitable for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, database operations, and moderate multi-threaded application hosting, offering a balanced resource distribution without the premium cost of specialized compute or memory-optimized hardware.
